blocks.text: After completing this module you will
- Understand the role of trust in entrepreneurial environment,
- Identify the core components of trust building (empathy, logic, authenticity),
- Recognize behaviours that strengthen or damage trust,
- Apply trust-building techniques in real life scenarios.

Trust building is a key competence that enables successfully navigating both informal, and entrepreneurial environments. It’s especially necessary in business settings, as the relationship based on trust needs to emerge both between the entrepreneur/company and customers, and between the businessman and resource providers. The reality of entering a new market space is full uncertainty and ambiguity, which can be addressed through building a connection based on trust. Therefore, being able to create such connections and maintain them becomes one of the crucial skills enabling the entrepreneur to thrive (Mickiewicz, Rebmann, 2019).

The ability to successfully build a trust-based relation with co-investors, suppliers or customers translates directly into the heightened potential of mutually beneficial cooperation. Example: you are preparing for the establishment of your new company and you’re looking for suppliers and investors. Due to the novelty of your proposal and unstable market environment, these actors might be reluctant or undecided to join you at first. Through the proper building of process-based trust (founded on actions), you will be able to reduce the ambiguity and uncertainty of the situation, and therefore to increase the chance to establish a long-lasting business relationship (Mickiewicz, Rebmann, 2019).
The following are the three fundamental components of trust building: (Frei, 2019)

items: Empathy - the process of trust building should start with genuine empathy expressed towards a given actor, as this feeling is expected to work as a catalyst for the rest of the trust-building process.
Logic - in order to be seen as trustworthy, the individual or a company needs to act and seem logical. People tend to pull back once they notice that the conveyed information isn’t sound.

Authenticity - the ability to always express your own self, regardless of different opinions or views of the people surrounding you. While in some cases it might seem risky, not being authentic carries way more trust-damaging potential.
Foster open dialogue at all times. Try to communicate with your associates and audience in an open manner, as often as you need to share something important.
Act on your values. Don’t only speak about your values but show your commitment to them by e.g. introducing relevant initiatives and informing customers about them.
Exceed expectations. Avoid over-promising and under-delivering, but do the opposite. People will appreciate you constantly delivering beyond promises.

Address issues with integrity. It’s normal to make a mistake or not meet some expectations. What people care about is how you handle such situations. Address each such occurrence with honesty, dignity and own up to it (Johannson, 2023).

blocks.text: Below we present the most significant challenges related to applying this skill (Frei, 2019):

items: The lack of time for empathy - due to the stressful and busy environment, we might often lack the time necessary to show empathy, thus building a connection. Analyze and identify your main distractors and try to avoid the most significant ones.

Explain your logic well - the reason for others not understanding your logic (a crucial component), might be your inability to express it well. To mitigate this challenge, try to start with explaining your point, and just then back it up with your reasoning.

blocks.text: Exercises
Below you can find two simple exercises to help you develop the skill of strategic thinking:

items: The trust map - draw the structure of your company / organisation / colleagues, and mark the current level of trust with each. Think about each connection and ask yourself “What’s one simple thing I can do this month to increase mutual trust?”

“Difficult situation” - imagine you have failed to deliver a big order of your product to a customer, who is now frustrated. You delayed your reply as well. Draft an email maintained in an honest, open, understanding tone, where you will acknowledge your mistakes, own up to what happened, offer the solution and reassure them about your commitment to further effective trust-based cooperation.

blocks.text: Answer each question with S or D. S = your area of strength; D = the area you should work on (Farmer Richards, 2025).

items: Am I empathetic and understanding in my interactions?
Am I reliable in my actions and words?
Do people around me feel they can depend on me?
How do I show that I am committed to the cause?
Am I clear and honest in my communication?
How do I deliver difficult news?

blocks.text: The skill of trust building is the crucial component of the effective entrepreneurial behaviour that will also benefit our personal lives, if applied correctly. The knowledge transferred over the pages of this chapter is expected to strengthen your overall understanding of the trust building’s importance in business settings, your ability to recognize its potential in specific situations, difficulties you might face when trying to apply this skill in real-life scenarios and ways of developing it. Creating a well-functioning enterprise requires all the necessary components, and building trust between you and your associates and customers is one of the most fundamental ingredients of success.
Learners who completed this module are expected to
- Be able to understand the significance of trust building in business relationships,
- Communicate in a manner fostering mutual trust building in professional settings,
- Analyze trust dynamics within their closest environment,
- Reflect on their own strengths and areas for improvement, in the context of this competence.

Books: Start With Why by Simon Sinek; The Speed of Trust: The One Thing That Changes Everything by Stephen M. R. Covey; The Trusted Advisor by David H. Maister, Charles H. Green, and Robert M. Galford
Videos: 7 Ways To Build & Earn Trust In 5 Minutes; The Trust Equation by David Maister explained: How to build trust; How Do We ACTUALLY Build Trust In Our Teams?
